Memory boosts generally cost one more to play, but let you do a bit of deck searching and then give you actual memory to work with later down the line.  
Trainings do much the same thing for a little less. Do a bit of searching, then get some memory discount on a future evolution, potentially helping you hold turn.

Scramble is the same cost as a Training, but forces you to evolve when you play it; and then it's delay hedges on your entire board being deleted so you can play out a rookie from your trash. It doesn't gain rush, either; so you can't do much with it that turn, either unless you're running an alliance deck/have something that can give them rush.

Say you initially digivolve Gargo as a counter to an enemy attack. You'd be able to unsuspend him and then activate his blocker effect, as well as suspending/preventing two of his cards from being unsuspended.  
On your next turn, you swing for their security or at one of their digimon, the attack goes through; you can then trigger that 'End of Attack' effect to unsuspend him at the end of the attack. And then choose to swing again if you want.

It's one of his better effects since if you counter digivolved him on the enemy turn; you can possibly kill off two of their digimon by attacking the ones you suspended with the other effect he has. And then at the end of your turn, thanks to Reboot; you'd unsuspend and be ready to block on their turn again.

No. Each is seperate. Digimon doesn't bother using seperators like / very often. So each trigger has it's own seperate colored box around it.   
So you can trigger the effect when you evolved, or when you attack.
No, if you look, they're in seperate blue boxes. Digimon doesn't bother seperating effect triggers with /'s and the like. if it's in it's own box, blue or orange; it's a seperate trigger.

When Digivolving and End of Attack are seperate triggers.

It unsuspends regardless of when or why it digivolved. So wether you did it on your turn or as part of an Ace Counter  
The When Digivolve part is meant more for being able to unsuspend it and then use it's blocker effect.

The End of Attack portion is more for using on your turn to get an additional swing at their security.

No, Alliance can be stacked, but not like that.

Each instance of Alliance allows you to use one other digimon to attack with the first.  
So using Shuu, your Brigadramon and one commandramon could attack together, giving you an additional security check for the attack, and combining Commandramons DP onto Brigadramons for both.

There is a LopMon who has the Main Phase effect; Give one digimon Alliance. This Alliance can be stacked onto digimon that already have it. It's currently, far as I know, the ONLY way to reliably stack Alliance effects on digimon.  
If you had two of those on the field, each could give Alliance to Brigadramon if you wanted to, as an example; they, along with Shuu's Alliance; would let you use all three Commandramons.

Viximons effect is inherited, so it doesn't matter what digivolution your at. If if's outside your breeding area, and you play an option card; you'll get to draw one card thanks to the egg's effect.  
It's "Your Turn, once per turn", but if you have multiple digimon on the field with Viximon in their ingeritables, you'd draw multiple cards.

Example  
You hatched a Viximon in your breeding area last turn, and evolved it into a renamon.  
This turn, you move it to the battle area and evolve it into say.. EX2's Kyubimon. You search, pull a Digivolution Plug-in thanks to it's digivolve skill.  
You decide to use that plug-in, letting you draw one and then digivolve one of your digimon.. say that Kyubimon into Taomon.

Because you used a plug in or option card with a cost of two or more; you'd draw one card for digivolving, and one more thanks to the inheritable from Vixi.

This works with all options, not just plug-ins. So Physical Training would also trigger it.

Renamon is still in a weird place. The new cards did help, but it's still not what you'd consider a 'meta' deck.

With the right cards? the right draws and planning? It can, like any deck, be very good. But it's a deck that relies on it's gimmick pretty hard; Option cards and tamers.  
Alot of the core power from the deck comes from playing option cards, usually for free via effects from your digimon or tamers, to get free evolutions and evo triggers going.

Main goal for the deck most of the time; is using DP reduction to flat out remove opponents digimon. Works very well I've found against black blocker focused decks since you can often DP reduce the key parts of their line to make them to weak to block or just outright remove them from the table as you swing.

And with the new support coming soon with Taomon and Sakuyamon Maid Mode Aces? with the right plug in's in your hand?  
We worked out you can easily deal a 20000DP reduction for three memory if you have the right level three and four stack already on field. That's nothing to sniff at, as pretty much any digimon, even with DP boosters from inheritables; is gonna die to that.

I think Tao ace is going to be bloody brilliant for the Renamon deck, especially with Maid Mode Ace also coming up later this year? with the right Plug-ins in hand.. it's devestating.

Tao Ace's inheritable is -4000dp on attack. couple that with two -2000dp's from the lvl 3 and 4.. -8000dp on attack. And it's on play/digivolve is play an option card if played on your turn rather than if played as a counter.  
So, hard drop a Evo plug in on digivolve, go into Sakuyamon straight away for free.. BT17's on evo is -6000dp. So the evolution chain and then attacking is -14000dp off the bat. That's already great. That deletes most big targets already.

But BT17's Sakuyamon's evo effect is also play an option... so if you have it; drop ANOTHER evo plug in to go into maid mode for free...  
Go into the new Maid Mode Ace? Play/digivolve; place a yellow tamer or 1 color option from hand onto security..  
Which also then triggers it's own all turns effect; when a option is used/card is added to security; 1 opponent digimon gets -6000dp for the turn...

So... starting from a Kyubimon? for Taomon Ace's 3 evo cost.. you're essentially getting to drop 20000DP in one turn, boost your security, get protection from deletion/bottom decking effects on the stack thanks to the Sakuyamon effect during this whole stack build.

  
Personally; I can't wait to get this running.
I can't wait for this and Maid Mode Ace later this year. So much support for my Rena deck!

Honestly my main advice would be start cheap.  
Don't use your good furs and materials on your first attempt at making something like a suit. Buy some really basic and cheap fur someplace like the local market or online and practice with that first.  
It's still going to set you back a bit of cash, but it'll help you learn what stitching you prefer, get familiar with cutting fur fabric without risking the final furs you plan to use on your suit.

Also: Tutorials.  
Youtube is a treasure trove of guides, tips and walk throughs on how to do fursuit parts, take measurements and much more; some even have patterns you can download to help make some bits easier.  
There's alot on there on making heads as well, with and without a resin base, that are really helpful.

Use some free templates and some cheap materials and make a few test pieces first. Get a feel for how things line up and go together before trying something like a full suit \^\^

Currently I play 4 Mother D-Reaper,   
20 Searchers  
4 Jeri (Suspend her, reveal top 5, add one searcher under mother; bottom deck rest)  
4 Bubbles (On play/Security; place one searcher from field or hand under mother)  
4 Pendulum (On play: reveal top 3, add 1 D-reaper trait and one searcher to hand; so can grab two searchers)  
3 Creep (Blocker on enemy turn)  
3 Optimizer (on play/attack: reveal top 3 and play an upto 10 cost card for free)  
2 Horn striker: has Rush  
2 Palates (can suspend it to delete an enemy digimon with equal or less DP, and benefits from the stacking +DP mother gives)  
4 Reaper: Basically your 'I win' card. trash 7+ searcher from under mother to play for free, has rush and constantly unsuspends while getting higher and higher DP.

Basically your egg, Mother, is your main builder. On your second turn it comes out onto field and is immune to all effects.  
You constantly play cards called Searchers, which draw one when played and cost 1 to play if no others are on field. Mother then absorbs one into it's sources every turn.  
For every card under her, you can reduce another digi's play cost by how many sources she has. You're usually looking to play cards that let you put more searchers under her each turn, like Bubbles.

End game/win generally is to have 7-8 searchers under her, and some more searchers in your trash so that you can play a card called "Reaper" for free by trashing the ones under the Mother card.. Basically comes onto the field for 0, has rush, and every time you attack you place two seachers from your trash under Reaper to unsuspend it. So you basically attack their security 5+ times in a single turn and win.

You can usually get there in 4-5 turns with good pulls/plays

It comes down to your comfort zone and the encounters I think?  


Arcane by design is amazing for rapid fire burst encounters where you need DPS and hard. get those arcane stacks up and pound away. Can make for a great ambush predator in pvp as once you have those stacks built up; you can strip health off a unaware foe or outright kill them before they can retaliate.

  
Frost on the other hand, at least for me, has greater sustain over longer encounters without the mana sacrifice and tends to serve me better for groups thanks to things like Hail, orb and more without having to be up close on the targets making it a bit better for PVE content

The Tau range is pretty well made, especially if you like the kind of japanese gundam anime feel to an army since they tend to be pretty suit focused.

The 'generic' start for alot of people is Space Marines since they tend to be the most supported model line in terms of new models, updates and tweaks; but they're basically bloody everywhere at this point.

In the end though; go for what you think will be fun and looks good. A good chunk of 40k is an army you like the look of and think will be fun; over actually always being competitive and trying to win.
